entry.name: vexpr
entry.digest: Evaluate a math expression for a list
entry.description: Performs mathematical calculations using C language-style mathematical operations. Operates on inputs that are lists rather than collections of single values.

arguments.name: expression
arguments.description: The argument to theobject is a mathematical expression composed of numbers, arithmetic operators such asor, comparisons such asor, C functions such asor, names ofobjects, and changeable arguments (,, and) for ints, floats, and symbols received in the inlets.

arguments.name: constant
arguments.description: Numbers can be used as constants in the mathematical expression.

arguments.name: format
arguments.digest: The data format for an inlets
arguments.description: Changeable arguments that specify data formats associated with an inlet are described using a combination of a data type (or) and an inlet number (example:). The argument will be replaced by numbers or symbols received in the specified inlet.

arguments.name: table
arguments.description: Changeable arguments that specify accessing data from a table are described using the argumentand an inlet number which is replaced by the name of ato be accessed. The argument should be immediately followed by a number in brackets specifying an address in the. (Examples:or.)

arguments.name: (other)
arguments.description: Theobject understands the following arithmetic operators:,,,, %. Other operators are(one's complement),(bitwise exclusive or),,,,, and(not).Many C language math functions can be understood by. A function must be followed immediately by parentheses containing any arguments necessary to the function. If the function requires a comma between arguments, the comma must be preceded by a backslash () so that Max will not be confused by it. For example:.C language functions understood byare: abs, min, max, sin, cos, tan, asin, acos, atan, atan2, sinh, cosh, tanh, int (convert to integer), float (convert to float), pow, sqrt, fact (factorial), exp (power of e to x), log10 (log), ln or log (natural log), and random. Additional functions can be added by means of external code resources placed in Max's startup folder.

messages.name: anything
messages.description: The items of each list are used individually, in order from left to right, to replace the changeable argument in a series of evaluations of the expression. When a list is received in the left inlet, the expression is first evaluated using the first item of each list, then using the second item of each list, etc. The series of results of these evaluations is then sent out as a list.

messages.name: bang
messages.description: Evaluates the expression and sends out the results, using the most recently received lists of numbers / symbols.

messages.name: float
messages.description: An int or float received in any inlet is treated as a single-item.
